messages:
priya: Kicked off KV-cache-only quantization bakeoff for llama-70b variant — comparing FP8 (mini-fp8) vs INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ) applied ONLY to the KV cache. We left weights at FP16 for stability. Posting summary + config + quick notes.

marta: TL;DR: both methods save substantial memory; INT8 wins on memory but costs a bit more latency. Quality delta tiny on our 2k eval set. See numbers below.

marta: Experiment setup: batch=8, seq=1024, p50/p95 measured on a reserved g5x (A100-like) pool, 100 warmup prompts + 1k eval prompts. We pinned model weights to fp16 and only quantized KV tensors.

marta: Config snippet used for runs (CLI):
```
--model llama-70b-merged
--batch 8
--seq-len 1024
--kv-quant-mode FP8        # values: NONE | FP8 | INT8-GPTQ | INT8-AWQ
--weights-quant none       # we kept weights at FP16
--kv-store ram            
--profile tokens 1000
```

marta: Raw comparative metrics (avg over 5 runs):
- Baseline (KV=FP16): KV mem = 32.0GB, p50 latency = 46ms, tokens/s = 215
- FP8 (KV): KV mem = 17.2GB (~-46%), p50 latency = 47.2ms (+2.6%), tokens/s = 210
- INT8 GPTQ (KV): KV mem = 14.1GB (~-56%), p50 latency = 49.2ms (+6.9%), tokens/s = 198
- INT8 AWQ (KV, experimental): KV mem = 13.7GB (~-57%), p50 latency = 51.5ms (+11.9%), instability on some long prompt patterns (see note)

priya: Quality checks: ran our 2k-sentence cross-task eval (summ, instruct, QA). eval-bot summary: avg token-loss delta vs baseline: FP8 +0.0009, INT8-GPTQ +0.0031, INT8-AWQ +0.0048. No statistically significant drop in top-1 correctness for our QA sets. chrF / BLEU differences within noise (<0.25 chrF).

eval-bot: Detailed eval output (key lines):
```
model baseline loss: 1.1248
fp8-kv loss: 1.1257  (delta +0.0009)
int8-gptq-kv loss: 1.1279 (delta +0.0031)
int8-awq-kv loss: 1.1293 (delta +0.0045)
```

ava: Noted an edge-case: INT8-AWQ runs showed hallucination rate increase on very long-context summarization (4/200 examples failed qualitatively). FP8 and GPTQ-INT8 were fine on those. AWQ also had occasional NaN during merge when using mixed-precision KV + fused kernels — likely implementation quirk on our runtime.

diego: Good catch. For Dedicated customers we need stable defaults. What's the operational knob to flip back to FP16 for KV if we see issues?

priya: We added runtime feature flag: --kv-quant-mode with safe-fallback. Policy in config:
```
kv_quant_mode: FP8
kv_quant_fallback: "FP16"  # auto-fallback if error or p95 degrades > 10%
kv_quant_check_interval: 300s
```
If the runtime detects NaN or p95 spike it will revert to FP16 for that connection and emit an alert to /eng-oncall.

theo: Can you attach the perf flame/log where the dequant step shows up? curious about CPU vs GPU overhead.

marta: Pasted micro profile (simplified):
```
baseline: matmul_kv    62% GPU
fp8:      dequant_kv   6% CPU, matmul_kv 60% GPU
int8:     dequant_kv  14% CPU, matmul_kv 58% GPU
awq:      dequant_kv  18% CPU, matmul_kv 56% GPU
```
Interpretation: FP8 uses a lighter-weight dequant path (tensor-core-friendly fp8 cast) so less CPU jitter; GPTQ-INT8 needs more dequant work on host/GPU and shows higher p95. AWQ currently has heavier unpack/merge overhead on our runtime which explains instability and p95.

priya: Notes on deployment profiles:
- Hosted (standard): default to FP8-KV for now (balanced memory reduction + low latency impact).
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs + predictable perf): expose INT8-GPTQ-KV as opt-in for customers that need max memory savings (saves ~45-55% KV memory).
- Private/on-prem: warn about AWQ instability and require runtime >= 2.3.1 and a canary phase.

ava: Recommendation: default FP8 for Hosted, offer INT8-GPTQ as "memory-saver" toggle in Console with an A/B rollout and health checks (we can auto-fallback). AWQ only as experimental flag for research customers.

diego: Any regression tests to gate this? We should add:
- perf smoke (p50/p95 within threshold)
- correctness suite (our 2k)
- NaN detection + KV-consistency checks
I'll add to eng-runtime 2 testcases.

priya: Action items:
- Marta: run 24h stability job for INT8-GPTQ on seq=32..8192 range and report memory/latency drift (assigned).
- Ava: debug AWQ NaN/merge flow and try trivial fix + re-run tiny-fuzz harness (assigned).
- Diego: wire the kv_quant_fallback into release 2.3.1 ops config and add alert.
- Theo: add perf flame sample to the PR and annotate dequant hotspots.

marta: I'll post the full CSV + raw traces in the drive link shortly. Quick note: for customers that need max dense context (>=32k) INT8-GPTQ-KV allowed us to push up to ~2x longer effective context before OOM on a 80GB GPU. That's probably the biggest practical win.

priya: Thanks all. If no blockers, we'll set hosted default to FP8-KV in the next non-breaking deploy and gate INT8-GPTQ behind console opt-in + rollout rules.

diego: :thumbsup:

ava: :sparkles: good job team
